summary: This rules resolution sets procedures for House floor consideration of three Clean Air Act amendment bills (on exceptional events data, EPA review of legislation, and foreign emissions) and a tax policy resolution, by waiving points of order, deeming each measure read, limiting debate to one hour, and allowing one motion to recommit.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural and makes no reference to appropriations, authorizations, or any form of government outlays. The underlying measures it advances also contain no spending provisions. Therefore the bill has no bearing on government spending.

Section 3 of the resolution provides for floor consideration of H. Res. 1156, a measure that expressly addresses tax policy. While the resolution itself does not enact tax changes, it directly facilitates debate on taxation, creating a tangential but clear connection to the topic.
No provisions in the resolution or the measures it makes in order relate to health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, or medical regulation. Score is therefore zero.
The bill text contains nothing concerning firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the resolution or the referenced bills.
The measure does not address reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations.
Neither the rules resolution nor the Clean Air Act or tax measures it advances contain any defense or military spending language.

Sections 2(a)–(c) provide for consideration of three bills that amend the Clean Air Act. H.R. 6387 alters handling of exceptional-event data and wildfire-mitigation actions; H.R. 6409 addresses treatment of foreign emissions; H.R. 6398 concerns EPA review of legislation. These changes adjust EPA regulatory processes in ways that typically reduce or clarify regulatory burdens, producing a moderate positive effect on the topic of limiting environmental regulations.
No welfare, SNAP, housing assistance, or entitlement provisions are present.

No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement appear.

No provisions touch on LGBTQ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
Foreign assistance is not addressed in any way.

No technology regulation, data privacy, or platform-liability language is present.
The resolution and referenced measures do not address collective bargaining, union rights, or labor standards.
No religious-exemption or anti-discrimination provisions appear.
